T h is appeal coming on for orders this day, t h e cou   following:
 ORDER

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 16.11.2022 passed by Member, M.A.C.T., Mandsaur in Claim Case No.117/2020 on Ashutosh vs M/S Paras Agency Through Partner Paras ... on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162125940/
1 account of inadequacy of the compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.
2 . The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability is not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in dispute.
As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of injured claimant, who suffered permanent disability, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,45,309/- along with interest.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has committed error in assessing the income of the claimant.

It is further submitted that the claimant is a B.Tech student and suffered permanent disability, so his income must be assessed as per the verdict of Madras High Court in the case of S.
Janakiraman Vs. R.Sekar and another C.M.A.No.3442/2019 decided on 22.06.2023.

entities.text:
S.
Janakiraman Vs. R.Sekar and another C.M.A.No.3442/2019 decided
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the matter.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contends that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the amount of compensation in the matter which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. On perusal of the evidence of the doctor who gave the permanent disability certificate to the claimant it is found that there is only 4.5% permanent disability, so the claimant is not entitled to get any compensation in regard to permanent disability.

6. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, more particularly the age of the claimant, his future prospects, in the considered opinion of this Court, the amount of compensation deserves to be enhanced by Rs.1,00,000/-.
7.
In the result, the appeal is allowed in part.
The enhanced amount i.e. Rs.1,00,000/- shall carry interest as awarded by the Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
